text: I’ll model the air volume as a rectangular box minus a 40 mm sphere centered at the origin. The box spans \(x=-5D\) to \(+15D\) and \(y,z=-5D\) to \(+5D\). I’ll mesh it with a coarse Cartesian `blockMesh`, then use `snappyHexMesh` to cut and refine the sphere and add prism layers. First I’m creating and measuring the CAD shape, then rendering a coarse geometric preview.

The preview showed the intended dimensions, but the CAD bounding-box measurement exposed a placement error: `Box` is center-aligned by default, so translating it by the minimum corner shifted the actual CAD volume. I’m correcting the primitive to use explicit minimum alignment and rechecking the true CAD bounds before meshing.

The corrected CAD now matches the requested extents and analytic volume. Next I’m inspecting the exact topological faces produced by the box subtraction so the named STL patches can be attached to CAD faces—not inferred later from mesh bounding boxes.

The subtraction produced exactly seven faces: inlet face 0, four far-field faces 1–4, outlet face 5, and the spherical cavity face 6. I’ll export these named patches together in one tessellation so all shared outer-domain edges remain welded.

I’ll use a 20 mm base Cartesian spacing (40×20×20 cells) for the coarse mesh, with three local refinement levels at the sphere (about 2.5 mm surface cells). The final mesh request includes five prism layers on `sphere`; I’ll use relative layer sizing with expansion ratio 1.2. The outer patch names are created directly in `blockMesh`, while the sphere patch comes from its named CAD surface.
The dictionaries are in place. I’m now generating only the coarse background mesh first and checking its patch topology before cutting the sphere.

`blockMesh` did not start because OpenFOAM requires a minimal `system/controlDict` even for meshing utilities. No mesh was generated. I’ll add that required case metadata, without solver or boundary-condition setup.
With the required case metadata present, I’m retrying the coarse background mesh generation.

The background mesh itself succeeded, but that cell was rejected from the reproducible script because `subprocess` came only from the earlier failed cell. I’m re-emitting the same single meshing step with its import explicit.

The coarse background mesh has 16,000 uniform hexahedra at 20 mm spacing and the three intended outer patches. I’ll now run `snappyHexMesh` to cut the sphere, refine its surface, and extrude the requested prism layers.
`snappyHexMesh` stopped immediately while reading case input, before altering the background mesh. I’m inspecting the captured error to identify the missing or invalid dictionary entry.

This OpenFOAM build also requires placeholder `fvSchemes` and `fvSolution` dictionaries when constructing the mesh object. I’ll add empty meshing-only dictionaries; no flow equations or boundary conditions are being configured.
The required mesh-object dictionaries are now present. I’m rerunning sphere snapping and layer extrusion.
The utility requires the standard scheme subdictionaries even though it does not solve equations. I’ll provide complete empty/default sections so mesh motion and quality code can initialize cleanly.
I’m retrying `snappyHexMesh` with the now-complete mesh-initialization dictionaries.

The coarse final mesh has 26,000 cells. All 744 sphere faces received all five requested layers, with 2.69 mm total prism thickness. I’m converting the mesh to VTK and rendering a center-plane cut so I can visually inspect the sphere cutout, local refinement, and layer stack.

The converted mesh contains exactly the four requested boundary patches. I’ll render both the full mid-plane and a close-up around the sphere; the close-up is necessary to see the prism layers rather than only the domain outline.

The full cut confirms the sphere is centered and refinement remains localized, but the linked camera prevented the second panel from zooming as intended. Before final validation, I’m measuring the meshed sphere directly from its boundary and checking its surface area against the analytic 40 mm sphere.

The snapped sphere measures 39.976×39.963×40.000 mm, with a 0.49% tessellated-area deficit—appropriate for this coarse surface mesh. I’m correcting the camera setup and making a dedicated close-up of the center-plane cells and layer stack.
The close-up now shows the concentric prism stack around the sphere and the graded transition to the 20 mm background grid. I’m running the binding bare `checkMesh` validation next.

The bare validation passes: 26,000 cells, one connected region, four patches, maximum non-orthogonality 35.9°, maximum skewness 0.538, and `Mesh OK`. The sphere patch is closed and all 744 surface faces have five layers. I did not run a flow solver or set boundary conditions, per scope.

The advisory gate confirms complete one-to-one patch coverage, so that warning is informational rather than a defect. It also reports the meshing point outside the sphere by 80.02 mm; that is intentional for an external-flow mesh—the retained region is outside the solid sphere and inside the outer box. I’m waiving both with those geometry-specific reasons.
